issues.t: Electric power steering assist cuts out (recall)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly gets very heavy, especially at parking-lot speeds, often with a 'Service Power Steering' message on the dash. It may come and go.
issues.why: The electric power steering motor and its torque sensor in the steering column can fail or lose signal. GM recalled many G6s for this (recalls 14V-153 and 15V-064), and the problem is the most reported complaint for this car.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the NHTSA or GM recall lookup. If the recall is open, a dealer fixes it free. If it was already done and the fault returns, the steering column motor or sensor usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Clunk or pop from the steering when turning
issues.sym: A clunk, pop or snapping feel in the steering wheel when turning at low speed, such as in parking lots. It can feel like the wheel catches for a moment.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft that links the column to the steering rack wears and binds. Worn tie rod ends or a worn steering rack can cause a similar noise.
issues.next: Have a shop check the intermediate shaft first, since it is the most common fix. Get it looked at soon if the steering ever feels loose or notchy.

issues.t: Replacement steering shaft can wear out early (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or looseness in the steering on a car that already had its intermediate steering shaft replaced. In the worst case steering control can be lost.
issues.why: Some service-replacement intermediate steering shafts were made with a yoke that does not support the joint bearing well, so they can wear out early (equipment recall 14E-044).
issues.next: If your steering shaft was ever replaced, ask a GM dealer to check whether the part is covered by this recall.

issues.t: Brake lights and shifter faults from the body module connector (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights that stay on or don't come on, cruise control that won't engage, the shifter stuck in Park, or traction and stability control warning lights.
issues.why: A connector at the body control module develops high resistance, which upsets the brake pedal switch signal. GM recalled 2005–2010 G6s (recall 14V-252).
issues.next: Check that your recall was done. A dealer cleans the connector, adds grease and resets the brake pedal sensor at no charge.

issues.t: Brake lights stay on or don't work from a corroded connector (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay lit when you are not braking, or don't light up when you press the pedal.
issues.why: Corrosion in a wiring connector for the brake lamp circuit can upset the signal (recall 09V-036).
issues.next: Make sure the recall was done. Until then, ask someone to watch the brake lights while you press the pedal.

issues.t: Shift cable can break, car may not stay in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park but the car rolls, the gear shown doesn't match the gear you are in, or the key won't come out.
issues.why: The transmission shift cable or the tabs on its end can break, or an adjuster clip may not be fully engaged. GM issued several recalls for this (14V-224, 12V-460 and 09V-073).
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the recall is checked. Have a dealer look up your VIN; the fix is free.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic loses 3rd, 5th and Reverse
issues.sym: The car suddenly won't go into Reverse, or skips gears and feels stuck in a lower gear. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: A wave plate inside the six-speed automatic can crack. GM extended coverage on this part to 10 years or 120,000 miles (bulletin 14404), and that coverage has now run out on these cars.
issues.next: Get the transmission diagnosed. If it is the wave plate, a shop can replace the clutch plate without swapping the whole transmission.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts hard or fails
issues.sym: Jolting or late shifts, especially between 20 and 40 mph, slipping, no pickup, or the transmission quitting altogether.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic used in most G6s wears internally. Owners report failures from about 45,000 to 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Get a scan for transmission codes before agreeing to a rebuild; a sensor or solenoid can sometimes be the cause.

issues.t: Low-beam headlights keep burning out or melting the plug
issues.sym: One or both low beams go dark, sometimes soon after a new bulb. The plug behind the headlight may be melted or brown.
issues.why: The headlight connector and wires overheat, which burns the plug and makes bulbs fail early. Hundreds of owners report it.
issues.next: Look at the plug when you change a bulb. If it is discolored or melted, replace the connector (pigtail) too, or the new bulb will fail.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle or tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine at startup, a check engine light for cam/crank timing, rough running, or in the worst case an engine that won't run.
issues.why: The 2.4L Ecotec's timing chain can stretch and its tensioner or guides can break, especially if oil changes were stretched out.
issues.next: Don't ignore a startup rattle or timing codes. Replacing the chain, guides and tensioner early is much cheaper than repairing engine damage.

issues.t: Check engine light from cam sensor or cam phaser solenoid
issues.sym: Check engine light, hesitation, rough idle or jerky shifts, sometimes with cam position codes.
issues.why: On the 2.4L, the camshaft position sensors and the cam timing (phaser) solenoids are known to fail.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A sensor or solenoid is a fairly cheap fix, but timing codes can also point to a stretched chain, so ask the shop to rule that out.

issues.t: Intake or head gasket coolant leak on the V6
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, oil leaks around the top of the engine, overheating, or milky oil in bad cases.
issues.why: The intake manifold and head gaskets on the 3.5L and 3.9L pushrod V6 engines can leak coolant or oil as they age.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and temperature gauge. Get a pressure test early; a leaking gasket left alone can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, low coolant warnings, or a rising temperature gauge.
issues.why: Water pump seals wear out, and several owners report replacing the pump between about 55,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Top up with the right coolant and get it fixed before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Clogged or failed catalytic converter
issues.sym: Check engine light, loss of power, poor fuel economy, a rotten-egg smell or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Several owners report the catalytic converter clogging or failing, sometimes after misfires or a rich-running engine.
issues.next: Fix any misfire first. Ask a dealer whether emissions warranty still applies, then have the converter tested.

issues.t: Retractable hardtop won't open or close
issues.sym: The folding hardtop stops partway, won't move, or shows a 'top not secure' style message. Squeaks and rattles from the roof are also common.
issues.why: The convertible's hardtop is complex, with many small switches, hydraulic cylinders and latches. Switches and sensors fail, and some parts are now discontinued.
issues.next: Don't force the top. A shop that knows these roofs can read the body codes to find which switch or cylinder is at fault.

issues.t: Front rotors warp early, brake pedal pulses
issues.sym: A shaking steering wheel or pulsing brake pedal when stopping, often well before the pads wear out.
issues.why: Owners report the front rotors warping or wearing unevenly on these cars.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and replaced (not just resurfaced if they are thin). Tighten wheel lugs by hand with a torque wrench to help prevent repeat warping.

issues.t: Clunking from the front suspension over bumps
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles from the front end over bumps or rough roads, sometimes with squeaks.
issues.why: Worn stabilizer bar end links and bushings, struts or control arm bushings are the usual causes.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. End links are cheap and often the cause; worn control arms or struts need sooner attention.

issues.t: Worn tie rod ends
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, uneven tire wear, or a clunk in the front.
issues.why: Tie rod ends are the single most-reported steering and suspension part in TrueDelta's owner survey for the G6.
issues.next: Have the steering linkage checked and get an alignment after any tie rod replacement.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing humming
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: The front wheel hub bearings wear out on these cars.
issues.next: Have the bearing checked; a badly worn bearing can get hot or loose.

issues.t: Starter failure
issues.sym: A click or nothing at all when you turn the key, even with a good battery.
issues.why: Starter motor failures are a common electrical complaint on the G6.
issues.next: Have the battery and cables tested first. If they are fine, the starter is likely bad.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the oil pan or valve cover gaskets
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell, or oil on the engine.
issues.why: Oil pan and valve cover gaskets harden with age and start to leak.
issues.next: Keep the oil level up and fix leaks that drip on hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Heater fan only works on some speeds
issues.sym: The blower works on high but not the lower settings, or stops and starts.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor or control fails.
issues.next: A blower resistor is a cheap part and usually the fix.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not turn off for a small child (recall)
issues.sym: No warning to the driver. The passenger airbag status light may show the airbag on with a child in the seat.
issues.why: The passenger sensing system may fail to turn off the front passenger airbag for some children in a crash (recall 07V-146).
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done. Children should always ride in the back seat.

issues.t: Aftermarket seat covers confuse the passenger airbag sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light acts up on cars with dealer-installed leather seat covers.
issues.why: Certain leather seat covers can make the passenger sensing system misread who is in the seat (recall 06V-417).
issues.next: Check whether the recall applies to your car with your VIN.

issues.t: Rear center child seat anchors and manual mismatch (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The manual says lower child-seat anchors are only at the outboard seats.
issues.why: The center rear lower anchors were placed differently from federal test rules, and the manual was wrong (recall 05V-098).
issues.next: Use the outboard rear seats for car seats with lower anchors and check the recall status.
